newsitem.title: JAPAN: Aramco Jan spot LPG awarded at $349-$358 - traders.
newsitem.headline: Aramco Jan spot LPG awarded at $349-$358 - traders.

text.p: State-owned oil firm Saudi Aramco has awarded its spot propane cargoes at around $349 per tonne and butane at about $358 in its first January tender to sell liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), traders said on Wednesday.

Aramco's contract prices for January are expected to be substantially higher than its December price of $310 for both propane and butane as the firm loosely works out its official selling prices according to the bids for its monthly tenders as well as its own assessments of spot market trends, they said.
Saudi Arabia's contract prices have a strong impact on the global LPG market as term prices for most LPG cargoes that originate east of the Suez are linked to Aramco prices.
Aramco's contract prices soared from $205 per tonne for October to $250 for November, the highest since the world's largest LPG supplier introduced the current pricing formula in October 1994.
Contract prices rose further to $310 for December loading for both propane and butane amid brisk demand from China and India as well as low inventories in the United States.
